Necromunda

Necromunda is a gang warfare skirmish game set in the underhive of a grimdark megacity, where rival gangs fight for territory, resources, and survival. Each gang — Goliath, Escher, Orlock, Delaque, Cawdor, and Van Saar — has its own playstyle and aesthetic. The game uses the same 32mm scale as Warhammer 40,000, and the industrial terrain is a major part of the experience.

32.0mm

Necromunda uses the same 32mm heroic scale as Warhammer 40,000. Gangers, hangers-on, and hired guns are all 32mm. The game features distinctive gang aesthetics — Goliaths are massive hulking brutes, Eschers are lean and fast, Van Saars are tech-heavy. Terrain (platforms, walkways, industrial machinery) is as important as the minis themselves.

Publisher: Games Workshop·Base Sizes: 25mm, 32mm, 40mm, 50mm, 65mm

Printing these minis on FDM

32mm gangers benefit from 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm layers for facial detail — Necromunda characters are individualistic and faces matter. Industrial terrain (gang hideouts, sector mechanicus platforms, pipe networks) prints beautifully on FDM at 0.1mm layers. The game's vertical terrain means you need a lot of it, so FDM is the practical choice for the board while resin handles the gangers.

All settings tested on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini with PLA. Your printer may want something different — always print a test piece first.

Frequently Asked Questions

What scale is Necromunda?
Necromunda miniatures are 32mm scale (1:50 ratio), measured eye level. Necromunda uses the same 32mm heroic scale as Warhammer 40,000. Gangers, hangers-on, and hired guns are all 32mm. The game features distinctive gang aesthetics — Goliaths are massive hulking brutes, Eschers are lean and fast, Van Saars are tech-heavy. Terrain (platforms, walkways, industrial machinery) is as important as the minis themselves.
What base sizes does Necromunda use?
Necromunda uses the following base sizes: 25mm, 32mm, 40mm, 50mm, 65mm.
What nozzle and layer height should I use for Necromunda miniatures?
32mm gangers benefit from 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm layers for facial detail — Necromunda characters are individualistic and faces matter. Industrial terrain (gang hideouts, sector mechanicus platforms, pipe networks) prints beautifully on FDM at 0.1mm layers. The game's vertical terrain means you need a lot of it, so FDM is the practical choice for the board while resin handles the gangers.
